    Does the military still use C-130?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, the AC-130 gunship is still in active service with the U.S. Air Force, with the AC-130J Ghostrider being the primary variant currently operating. It serves as a heavily armed, long-endurance aircraft specializing in close air support and armed reconnaissance, with plans to keep it operational for decades. 
    • Current Variant: The Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) operates around 31 AC-130J Ghostriders, which replaced older variants like the AC-130U "Spooky".
    • Armament: The AC-130J is armed with a 105mm howitzer, a 30mm GAU-23/A autocannon, and precision-guided munitions (missiles and bombs).
    • Role:
      While designed for counterinsurgency and special operations in permissive environments, the AC-130 is being adapted for potential high-end conflicts.
    • Recent Usage: The platform remains actively deployed for combat missions, with recent operations including strikes in the Middle East.

      AI Overview
      +9
      The Lockheed C-130 Hercules is a versatile four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft, designed for tactical airlift, medevac, and cargo transport from unprepared runways. Produced for over 70 years, it is used by over 70 countries for diverse roles including gunship (AC-130), search and rescue, and firefighting. 
      Key Features and Performance 
      • Maximum Speed: The C-130J Super Hercules cruises at high speeds, often listed around 417 mph (Mach 0.59) at 22,000 feet.
      • Range: The C-130J offers enhanced range, with the capability to operate in diverse theaters of operations
        .
      • Seating/Capacity: The C-130 can carry over 90 combat troops, approximately 64 paratroopers, or a max payload of over 40,000 pounds.
      • Variants: The platform has over 70 variants, with the C-130J being the current standard. 
      History 
      • Development: The US Air Force requested the design in 1951, with the first production model, the C-130A, taking flight shortly after.
      • Longevity: Originally designed for troop and cargo transport, the C-130 has been in continuous production and service for over 70 years.
      • Modernization: The C-130J Super Hercules is the current, modernized iteration, featuring a new flight deck, engines, and improved performance. 
      Operational Use 
      • Versatility: C-130s are used for worldwide humanitarian aid, air support, weather observation, and as aerial command centers.
      • Combat: The aircraft has been vital in transporting troops and supplies in every U.S. conflict since the mid-20th century, notably in Iraq and Afghanistan.
      • Firefighting: The C-130H is used by organizations like CalFire for dropping fire retardant, with a capacity of 4,000 gallons. 
      While specific pricing for military aircraft varies based on contracts, the C-130J is a highly exported, modern platform produced by Lockheed Martin.

      The Lockheed C-130 Hercules is an American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft designed and built by Lockheed. Capable of using unprepared runways for takeoffs and landings, the C-130 was designed as a troop, medevac, and cargo transport aircraft.
